proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains no indemnity at all, so we have added the Contractor indemnity our playbook requires for third-party IP infringement claims, Contractor's breach of law, Contractor-caused compromise of Company data, and Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a carve-out from the Section 7(a) cap. If you cannot accept an uncapped indemnity, we can discuss customary IP exclusions (Company modifications, combinations and specifications), the usual procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and a super-cap of 3x annual fees.

ops.text: (d) INDEMNIFICATION BY CONTRACTOR. Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or the Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information or data caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of the claim, Contractor shall have control of the defense and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or admission on Company shall be made without Company's prior written consent), and Company shall provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense. Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d) are not subject to the limitations set forth in Sections 7(a), 7(b) and 7(c).

proposal.summary: Insert Contractor (Vendor) indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard defence procedure and carve-out from the liability cap.

quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but its three subsections contain only liability caps (7(a)), a consequential damages waiver (7(b)) and an attorneys' fees waiver (7(c)); a document-wide search for "indemn", "hold harmless" and "defend" returns no operative indemnity language anywhere. Contractor's IP non-infringement warranty in Section 5(c) is not backed by any defence or indemnity obligation, so Clear Capital bears the cost of third-party infringement claims, Contractor-caused data breaches and Contractor's misconduct. This is the walk-away scenario (no Vendor IP indemnity at all), so we insert the playbook Vendor indemnity as new Section 7(d), with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a carve-out from the Section 7 caps. No Customer indemnity exists that needs narrowing.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for and everything we put in, so we have made ownership of the Works vest in us on creation with an express assignment rather than being conditioned on invoices having been paid (our payment protection is the fee and termination provisions, not IP title). We have also confirmed that our data and pre-existing IP remain ours with no assignment to Contractor and no joint ownership, and made the licence to Contractor's Information embedded in the Works irrevocable and worldwide so we can keep using the Works after the engagement ends.

ops.newText: are the property of Company upon creation, and Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns to Company all right, title and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Works, effective upon creation and regardless of whether any invoice for the related Services has then been issued or paid.

ops.text: (e) Company retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, content, materials, software and other intellectual property provided or made available by Company, or generated for or on behalf of Company, in connection with the Services ("Company Data"), and nothing in this Agreement operates as an assignment, transfer or licence (other than a licence to Contractor to use Company Data solely as necessary to perform the Services) of any Company Data or Company intellectual property to Contractor. Nothing in this Agreement creates joint ownership of the Works or Company Data.

proposal.summary: Works vest in Company on creation with an express assignment; add Company Data/pre-existing IP ownership and no joint ownership; make the embedded-Contractor-IP licence irrevocable and worldwide.

quote: are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid.
rationale: Section 4(a) makes our ownership of the Works contingent on the relevant invoice having been issued and paid, so title in work product we commissioned does not vest on creation and there is no present assignment from Contractor — leaving Contractor as owner of unpaid-for deliverables and requiring only "reasonably required assistance" at our cost. The Agreement also contains no provision confirming that Clear Capital retains ownership of its own data and pre-existing IP (our data is addressed only as Confidential Information in § 8), and no bar on joint ownership. The licence back in § 4(c) for Contractor's Information embedded in the Works is perpetual and royalty-free but not irrevocable or worldwide, falling short of the preferred position. Contractor's retention of its own proprietary tools and methodologies under § 4(b) is acceptable and left intact. Redline: vest the Works in us on creation with an express irrevocable assignment, add a Company Data / pre-existing IP ownership and no-joint-ownership provision, and make the embedded-IP licence irrevocable and worldwide.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the cap mutual and set it at the greater of the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim and USD 1,000,000, replacing the open-ended "fees paid for such Services" basis and the cross-reference to Paragraph 9 (which is the independent contractor clause, not an indemnity). Our position is that confidentiality, data protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP sit outside the cap, and that our payment obligations are not "damages"; if helpful, we can fall back to a mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs at least for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

ops.newText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY COMPANY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE CONSIDERED DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THE FOREGOING LIMITATION.
ops.oldText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 and add standard uncapped carve-outs

quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7(a) caps liability at "fees paid" — for the Contractor, only the fees paid for the particular Services under the relevant SOW, which can be a very small amount and is measured on a "paid" (not "paid or payable") basis with no 12-month or USD floor. The only carve-out points to "Paragraph 9", which is the Independent Contractor clause (there is no indemnification provision in the agreement despite the section heading), so the carve-out is illusory and confidentiality breaches (Section 8), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all sit inside the cap. The cap is also drafted asymmetrically in the Contractor's favour and Clear Capital's payment obligations are not excluded from "damages". Redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the standard Excluded Claims carve-outs, and confirms fee payment obligations are not capped damages. The mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages in 7(b) already meets the playbook and is left unchanged.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a carve-out so Clear Capital can assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and confirmed that a change of control of Clear Capital gives Contractor no termination or re-pricing right. Our playbook does not permit our corporate reorganizations to be gated by vendor consent; if helpful, we can accept a mutual notice-based successor assignment right as a fallback.

ops.newText: without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld; provided, however, that Company may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without Contractor's consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business, and no change of control of Company shall be deemed an assignment or give Contractor any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement or any Statement of Work. Contractor shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Company.
ops.oldText: without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add Company affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, bar assignment to a Company competitor, and confirm no Contractor right arising from Company change of control

quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: Section 7's clause 10 imposes a symmetrical consent requirement on any assignment or transfer, with no carve-out permitting Clear Capital to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and no bar on Contractor assigning to a Clear Capital competitor. The "not unreasonably withheld" standard keeps this above walk-away (it is not a blanket prohibition), but it still gates our corporate reorganizations on RadialSpark's consent. No change-of-control termination right exists (Section 6 termination rights are notice/breach based), so we only add confirming language that a change of control is not an assignment and creates no Contractor termination or re-pricing right. Redline validated ok:true.

quote: Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement.
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Clear Capital. The engagement is expressly "on a task by task basis" through individual Statements of Work (p0004), compensation is time-and-materials with no minimum volume or requirements commitment (p0013), and there is no language requiring Company to purchase all or any share of its requirements from Contractor or barring it from procuring similar services from third parties (searches for "exclusive", "sole supplier/provider", "requirements", "competing", "non-compete" returned no such covenant). The only "sole and exclusive" references are Contractor's ownership of its pre-existing property (p0020) and the standard non-exclusive license and entire-agreement clauses (p0021, p0051), which are IP/boilerplate rather than exclusive dealing. The mutual non-solicitation of employees (p0047) is a personnel restriction, not a restriction on sourcing services. Our freedom to buy from other suppliers is preserved, so no redline is needed.

quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties, stipulated sums or early-termination/minimum fees are payable by Clear Capital anywhere in the Agreement. Section 3 (compensation) provides only for time-and-materials fees, reimbursable expenses and taxes, with no late-payment penalty or interest; Sections 6(a)/(b) and the duplicate 7(c) termination provision entitle RadialSpark only to fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the termination date, which is compensatory rather than a liquidated amount. Section 7 contains only mutual liability caps and a consequential-damages waiver, and searches for "liquidated damages", "penalt", "minimum" and "interest" return no Customer-payable stipulated sums. As a direction rule, nothing runs against us, so the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) is already met and no redline is needed.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended this licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and made it irrevocable and transferable to a successor, so the delivered Works remain usable across our group and after any reorganisation. If preferred, we can instead cover affiliates on written notice with transfer limited to a successor in an M&A transaction.

ops.newText: Contractor hereby grants to Company, its affiliates (any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Company) and contractors acting on Company's behalf a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable license, transferable to a successor to Company's business or assets (including the right to grant a sublicense)
ops.oldText: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense)

proposal.summary: Extend Contractor's Information licence to Company affiliates and contractors, make it irrevocable and transferable to a successor.

quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: The only licence grant (Section 4(c), covering Contractor's Information embedded in the Works) runs to "Company" alone: affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not named, the grant is not stated to be irrevocable, and it is not transferable (Section 10 bars assignment without consent, so no successor path). It is perpetual and includes sublicence rights, so the gap is narrower than walk-away, but it falls short of the preferred position. Redline adds affiliates and contractors, "irrevocable", and transferability to a successor to our business or assets; fallback is affiliate coverage on notice with M&A successor transfer only.

quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: We reviewed the full agreement (preamble, §§ 1-7 and the numbered clauses 8-19) for any covenant limiting Clear Capital's business lines, products or fields of use. There is no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding us: the only restrictive covenant is the mutual employee non-solicitation in clause 13, which is reciprocal, term-plus-one-year and confined to personnel involved in the Services, and therefore outside the scope of this rule. The only other "Company shall not" language, in § 4(b)(ii) (p0020), bars resale or unrelated use of Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials and administrative records — an IP licence-scope limit on Contractor's property, not a restraint on our business, and it is mitigated by the perpetual, sublicensable licence to Contractor's Information for our business operations in § 4(c). Section 4(b) (p0019) likewise runs the other way, preserving Contractor's freedom to serve other clients rather than restricting us. No redline required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a clear right to exit for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, including while a Statement of Work is running, and Contractor's convenience right should not allow it to walk away from active work on 15 days' notice. As a fallback we can accept 60 days' notice for Company, but Contractor's convenience right must remain limited to periods with no outstanding Statement of Work on 90 days' notice.

ops.newText: (a) Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Company shall have no early termination charge or other penalty. Contractor may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason only at a time when there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, upon ninety (90) days advance written notice to Company.
ops.oldText: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.

proposal.summary: Give Company a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund; limit Contractor's convenience right to when no SOW is outstanding on 90 days' notice.

quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
rationale: Section 6(a) conditions any convenience termination on there being no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, so Company has no convenience exit while work (and prepaid fees) are live, and it says nothing about refunding prepaid amounts. At the same time it gives Contractor a symmetric convenience right on only fifteen (15) days' notice, which is below the playbook walk-away threshold of 90 days. The redline gives Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW with a pro-rata refund and no penalty, and confines Contractor's convenience right to periods with no outstanding SOW on 90 days' notice.

quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work.
rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or fee-verification right exercisable by RadialSpark against Clear Capital. Section 3 (Compensation) imposes invoicing/supporting-detail obligations on the Contractor only and gives it no right to audit our usage, books or records; Sections 4 and 7 likewise contain no verification right, and the only systems-access language (p0007) runs in our favor by requiring Contractor personnel to comply with Company access and security policies. Because the AUDIT rule constrains audit rights binding the Customer and none exist, the position is satisfied without edits; no redline is proposed since adding an audit framework would create a right the Vendor does not currently have.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved governing law from Arizona to New York and replaced binding arbitration with the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with our standard position that disputes be resolved in court under New York law. If New York is difficult, we can accept Delaware or California law and courts as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Change governing law from Arizona to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the New York County courts.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
rationale: The agreement selects Arizona law, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and specifies no court venue. Section 19 further mandates binding arbitration of all disputes under U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules, whereas our position requires resolution in courts. We therefore changed the governing law to New York and substituted exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County for the arbitration forum, leaving the remainder of both clauses intact. Not a walk-away, as the arbitration seat is domestic rather than foreign.

quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
rationale: Section 3 (Contractor's Compensation) is the only pricing provision and sets time-and-materials compensation, expense reimbursement, invoicing and taxes, with rates fixed by each Statement of Work (subject only to Contractor's right to change rates on 30 days' notice). Full-text searches for MFN-type language ("most favoured/favorable", "no less favorable", "best", third-party price matching) returned no results anywhere in the Agreement. There is therefore no obligation requiring Clear Capital to extend to RadialSpark terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, which satisfies the preferred position (no MFN burden on Customer). No Vendor-granted MFN exists either, but that is a nice-to-have rather than a rule breach, so no redline is warranted.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "retainer", "non-refundable", "guaranteed" and "volume" return no commitment language binding Clear Capital. Compensation under § 3(a) is purely time-and-materials for Services actually ordered under a Statement of Work (§ 1(a) engages Contractor "on a task by task basis"), and § 3(b) invoicing is based on hours actually worked. Section 6(a) also permits either party to terminate for convenience on 15 days' notice when no Statement of Work is outstanding, and § 6(b) limits Contractor's recovery on termination to fees "incurred or earned" through the termination date — no shortfall or penalty exposure. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for ordered services only), so no redline is needed.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept a mutual, narrowly scoped non-solicit, but we need the standard carve-outs so ordinary hiring activity is not caught: general advertisements and job postings not targeted at the other party's personnel, and responses to unsolicited approaches. This keeps the clause at our fallback position without changing its 12-month duration or its limitation to personnel directly involved in the Services.

ops.newText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this section shall restrict either party from (i) placing general advertisements or job postings not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or hiring any person who responds to such advertisements or postings, or (ii) hiring any person who approaches that party on an unsolicited basis or who is no longer employed or engaged by the other party.

quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: Section 13 binds Clear Capital (as well as RadialSpark) to a non-solicit. It is already close to our fallback: mutual, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, and only 12 months post-termination, with no no-hire prohibition (it restricts soliciting for hire, not hiring as such). The single gap is the absence of carve-outs for general advertisements/job postings and unsolicited approaches, which our playbook requires. Because the clause is mutual and narrowly scoped, insisting on the preferred position (no non-solicit at all) is disproportionate; we propose the minimal fallback edit adding the carve-out sentence.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs on an evergreen term, so we have added predictability to pricing: rates are fixed for the duration of each Statement of Work and any later increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 60 days' notice, consistent with our position that continuing engagements be priced predictably. If helpful, we can accept a 5% cap as a fallback.

ops.newText: Rates set forth in a Statement of Work are fixed for the duration of that Statement of Work. Thereafter, Contractor may increase rates no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, effective no earlier than sixty (60) days after written notice to Company, and no such increase shall exceed the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI-U, All Items) over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%).
ops.oldText: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.

proposal.summary: Cap Contractor's unilateral rate increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, once per 12 months, with 60 days' notice; rates fixed during each SOW.

quote: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.
rationale: There is no automatic renewal mechanic: § 2 (p0011) creates an evergreen term continuing "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6," and § 6(a) lets either party (including us) exit on fifteen (15) days' notice, so the renewal-term and non-renewal-notice-window limbs of the rule are satisfied (no notice window, no multi-year renewal). The price-predictability limb is not: § 3(b) lets Contractor unilaterally change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap and no frequency limit, which on an open-ended term produces exactly the uncontrolled uplift the rule guards against. We propose fixing rates for the duration of each Statement of Work and capping any subsequent increase at the lesser of CPI and 3%, once per twelve months, on 60 days' notice; a 5% cap is the fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a standard exit clause: on expiry or termination Contractor provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data, Works and Confidential Information within 30 days in a machine-readable format, and then deletes and certifies deletion. The Agreement is otherwise silent on exit, which would leave our data and in-flight work stranded; we can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Company all Works, Company data and Confidential Information in Contractor's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all such Works, Company data and Confidential Information from its systems (other than Contractor's Information as described in Section 4(b)) and certify such deletion to Company in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations in Section 6

quote: (c) In the event of termination under either section 6(a) or 6(b) of this agreement, Contractor shall be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Upon receipt of final payment Contractor shall provide to Company, and will assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.
rationale: Section 6 (with the related clause (c) at p0044) addresses only notice, final fees and assignment of Works in progress. There is no obligation on Contractor to provide transition assistance, to return Company data/Confidential Information in a usable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards; Section 8 restricts use/disclosure of Confidential Information but requires no return or destruction. This is a services/development engagement where our data and work product sit with Contractor, so the playbook's exit protections are absent and inserted as new Section 6(d) (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion), carved back for Contractor's Information under Section 4(b).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5 gives us authority, IP and anti-bribery warranties but no warranty that the Services and Works will actually conform to the Specifications, and no remedy if they do not. We have added a standard performance and conformity warranty (12 months for Works, professional and workmanlike Services), a no-malicious-code warranty, and a repair/re-perform/replace-or-refund remedy, and confirmed that the disclaimer in 5(e) does not cut back these express warranties. If 12 months is too long for your delivery model, we can accept 90 days for the Works and 30 days for Services with the same remedies.

ops.text: (f) Contractor represents and warrants to Company that: (i) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (ii) for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery, each of the Works will conform in all material respects to the applicable Specifications and documentation; and (iii) the Works will not contain any virus, worm, malicious code or other routine designed to disable, damage or permit unauthorized access to the Works or Company's systems. For breach of the warranty in clause (ii) or (iii), Contractor shall, at Company's request, promptly repair or replace the non-conforming Works or re-perform the affected Services and, if Contractor fails to do so within thirty (30) days, refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Works or Services. Nothing in Paragraph 5(e) limits or disclaims the express warranties set forth in this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add express conformity/workmanship/no-malicious-code warranty with repair-replace-reperform-or-refund remedy, and confirm the disclaimer does not swallow it

quote: (e) THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
rationale: Section 5 contains only legal-compliance, authority, non-infringement and anti-bribery warranties. There is no express warranty that the Services or the Works will conform to the Specifications or documentation, no warranty period, no no-malicious-code warranty, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; the only performance standard is the bare covenant in 1(b), which carries no stated remedy. Combined with the implied-warranty disclaimer in 5(e), Company is left without a meaningful conformance warranty, short of the playbook preferred position (12 months software / 90 days services with repair, replace or refund). Redline inserts a new 5(f) with the workmanship, conformity and malicious-code warranties, the remedy, and a confirmation that 5(e) does not swallow the express warranties; fallback of 90/30 days offered in the comment.

rationale: An insurance clause exists (Section 14), so the rule is not missing, but it falls short of the preferred position in three respects: no CGL aggregate limit, E&O at USD 1M rather than USD 2M, and no cyber/privacy liability cover at all. Cyber cover is squarely relevant here because Contractor obtains Company Confidential Information including data and records (p0038), may access Company computer systems and works at Company facilities (p0007). Workers' compensation as required by statute and certificates on request are already satisfied. The redline raises E&O to USD 2M, adds the USD 2M CGL aggregate and USD 5M cyber/privacy cover, and extends the coverage period one year beyond the term consistent with our model language; fallback (E&O USD 1M plus cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment.
